Beyond that, the create response does not match the ShareLink contract the button consumes, the button is not mounted anywhere, and errors from rand.Read and Links().Save are ignored. The token design itself follows the settled decision and the diff stays within scope (no expiry UI). | BLOCKS (blocker/high): share.Register is never called. routes.go only registers schedules.Register(r) and nothing else in the repo references the share package, so POST /schedules/:id/share and GET /share/:token do not exist on the running API. The handlers are dead code and the feature is unreachable. | BLOCKS (blocker/high): `make test` runs `true`, so the verify output "ok" executes no Go or web tests at all. No acceptance criterion has real test evidence; every "(test)" is unproven. | BLOCKS (major/medium): The tests use assertStatus, post, get, owner, stranger and tok, none of which are defined anywhere in the share package or the repo; Router and Ctx are also undefined in package share. The package would likely not compile if the tests were actually run. | BLOCKS (major/medium): Create returns only {"token"}, but the contract type ShareLink (packages/contract/src/share.ts:1) requires token, scheduleId and expiresAt, and ShareButton renders link.expiresAt. With the real response the button would read "valid until undefined". Links().Save(tok, s.ID) is also given no expiry although Get checks l.Expired(). | BLOCKS (major/medium): ShareButton is not imported or rendered anywhere, and nothing in the web app calls POST /schedules/:id/share to obtain a link, so a user has no way to reach the button. The copied URL is `${location.origin}/share/<token>` on the web origin, but there is no web route or page for /share/:token, only the API route, so the copied link may lead nowhere. | BLOCKS (major/medium): The test uses render, screen and click without importing them, and never mocks navigator.clipboard.writeText, so toHaveBeenCalledWith would fail on a non-mock unless global setup exists (none is in the repo). | BLOCKS (major/high): Errors from rand.Read and c.Links().Save are discarded. A failed save still returns 201 with a token that will 404; a failed rand.Read would yield an all-zero, guessable token.

trials.label: revise
trials.detail:
[fable/medium] The plan does not reach done as written: no task owns apps/api/internal/http/routes.go, so share.Register is never wired into http.Register. Both endpoints would return 404 in the real app while every package-level test passes. The acceptance criterion for the 405 through the real router is also in no task's done, and routes_test.go has no owner. Giving both files to the api task, with real-router tests, fixes this.

The rest is sound: the contract, storage and token decisions match the ADR and the existing code, the web and api tasks don't collide, and no migration is needed. The remaining findings are smaller gaps: what the owner sees after clicking Share, clipboard failure, store-error and missing-schedule paths on the public GET, and the non-404 error state on the public page. | BLOCKS (blocker/high): No task owns routes.go, so share.Register is never called from http.Register. The api task owns only apps/api/internal/share/**, and http.Register (the function the real server uses) calls only schedules.Register. Handler tests in the share package would still pass, because testutil.NewServer accepts share.Register directly, so `make test` would be green while both endpoints return 404 in the real app. The Share button and the public page would have nothing to call. | BLOCKS (major/high): The acceptance criterion "Only GET is routed for /share/:token: POST to it returns 405 (api test through the real router)" appears in no task's done, and the file where such a test belongs is owned by nobody. The api task's done lists only handler tests, so nobody will write or be checked on this test. | BLOCKS (major/medium): The plan says the button "copies the returned url" but names no visible result on success and no behaviour when the clipboard is unavailable. navigator.clipboard.writeText can reject (insecure context, permission denied). The owner could click Share and see nothing, which misses "get a link". The done criterion's error case covers only a failed POST.

trials.label: proceed
trials.detail:
[fable/high escalated] The plan is sound against the code and can run as written. Nothing blocks; the five findings are minor and I raised the bar on six criteria.

- **Coverage:** every acceptance criterion maps to a task, and routes.go, routes_test.go and routes.tsx are each owned, so nothing is left unwired.
- **Code fit:** the pieces the plan leans on already exist: `auth.Require` (401), `schedules.PublicView`, `store.KV`, `config.WebOrigin`, the router's built-in 405 for unrouted methods, contract `ScheduleView`, and the `isOwner` slot in SchedulePage.
- **Ordering:** api and web own disjoint files and both wait only on contract, so they can run in parallel without colliding.
- **Decisions and scope:** the decisions match ADR 0007, and no task builds anything a non-goal rules out.
- **Findings:** per-task verify lists omit `make lint`, testutil is owned by nobody, repeat-POST behaviour is unwritten, WEB_ORIGIN is not normalised, and main.tsx is not in the repo to check for an auth wrapper.
- **Raised bar:** exact ShareLink JSON keys, no ownerId in the public body plus a signed-in non-owner viewer, dangling-token and KV-failure paths, the url shown on screen with clipboard failure handled, read-only and non-404 handling on the shared page, and both anonymous and non-owner cases for the hidden button.

I could not run anything; the baseline pass is taken as given.
